05 / PRODUCT

A world teens
would choose.

The product question: can a fantasy class earn attention through its characters, creative activity and sense of place?

THE RESEARCH, DIGESTED

Belonging. Expression.
Something worth doing.

Our existing 20-game research set points to useful patterns to test: personal identity, social context, clear goals, and the satisfaction of making something. These are design judgments informed by research, not proven causes of success.

Research cutoff: October 29, 2026. The study combines youth surveys, all-age Roblox activity and mobile/commercial signals. It is not a unified popularity ranking of US players aged 13–17. Royale High is an additional thematic reference outside the 20-game set.

SIX USEFUL COMPARISONS

What we take forward.

Study the principle.
Give VRHS its own visual answer.

ReferenceUseful lensObservation to testVRHS art decision
Royale High ↗Place & belongingAn academy can offer identity as well as activities.Memorable department landmarks within a coherent campus.
Brawl Stars ↗Clarity & characterReadable silhouettes and concrete objectives reduce explanation.Distinct teacher shapes and a teaching prop visible at small size.
Adopt Me! ↗Warmth & attachmentFriendly forms and personal spaces can encourage a sense of ownership.Approachable mentors with enough costume and attitude for teens.
Dress To Impress ↗Expression & presentationA clear creative prompt makes different responses easy to showcase.A well-lit stage for student work, with useful feedback.
Minecraft ↗Making & modularityA small construction vocabulary can support many personal outcomes.Reusable environment kits and choices that change something visible.
Genshin Impact ↗Composition & discoveryLandmarks and layered views make a world feel worth exploring.One strong vista and deliberate focal depth at a much smaller scope.

COMMERCIAL QUESTIONS

A clear promise.
A testable next step.

The intended first audience is teens 13–17. Who chooses the experience, who pays, and what brings a player back remain product hypotheses.

Before expanding the campus, test whether the character and activity make a student want another class. A monetization model has not been validated.

The first things to learn

  1. Does the look feel distinctive, welcoming and age-appropriate?
  2. Can a fresh player understand the next action without coaching?
  3. Does the player recognize what their choice changed?
  4. Would they choose to try another class or show a friend?

Playtest results forthcoming.

SELECTED EVIDENCE

Keep the evidence
in proportion.

JIM youth survey 2025 ↗Germany, ages 12–19. Useful youth preference evidence; a different population from US teens 13–17.

Norwegian Media Authority, 2026 ↗Mixed youth age groups in Norway. Regional and age differences matter.

Sensor Tower, September 2026 ↗Commercial and download context without teen age segmentation.

Digest adapted from the VRHS research prepared October 29. Game comparisons are creative/product analysis. Current raw statistics are deliberately omitted here; popularity does not establish learning value.
